title: SportVot gives Liga Portugal trio coverage in India, Sri Lanka, Maldives
article_text:
Portuguese soccer’s top-tier Liga Portugal has increased its international visibility by securing SportVot, the live sports streaming platform, as a new broadcast partner in India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives.

The new agreement sees SportVot secure exclusive streaming rights to league matches involving Liga Portugal’s three most renowned clubs – Sporting CP, Benfica, and FC Porto – which it will air on its platform.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The deal was brokered by international sports marketing agency Sportfive, which serves as the league’s international media rights partner through 2027-28. The deal covers global markets outside Portugal ahead of Liga Portugal’s transition to a centralized rights model starting in 2028-29.

Shubhangi Gupta, co-founder of SportVot, said, "Football has a passionate and growing audience across India and South Asia, and we're excited to bring matches featuring clubs like Sporting CP, Benfica and FC Porto to fans in these markets.

“Acquiring these rights is an important step in building SportVot's international content portfolio and making more quality live sporting action accessible to audiences through our platform."

The deal marks the first time Indian audiences will have access to Liga Portugal matches through a dedicated streaming platform and opens the league up to a potentially lucrative new market.

The deal is the latest move by SportVot to pivot beyond domestic and emerging sports and into premium sports content, having earlier this year secured exclusive streaming rights in India for 2026 summer club friendlies, covering pre-season matches across the Premier League, LaLiga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, and Liga Portugal.

Meanwhile, the new agreement comes as Liga Portugal looks to boost its international visibility, having yesterday announced a rights deal in Australia with nascent digital soccer platform Football360 for the remainder of the 2026-27 season.

Under its agreement, Football360 will stream two matches per week via its website, as well as replays on demand, mini matches, highlights, and short-form video content across its website and social media channels.

Earlier this year, international OTT sports streaming service DAZN acquired rights to show three Liga Portugal matches per game week for the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons exclusively in Japan, Italy, and Belgium and non-exclusively in Spain.

Shortly after, German sports channel Sportdigital extended its exclusive broadcast rights to Liga Portugal through the 2027-28 season.

title: Sports Direct Signs Major Five-Year Deal with Shamrock Rovers
article_text:
Shamrock Rovers have confirmed a major new commercial partnership with Sports Direct Ireland, which will become the club’s official front-of-shirt sponsor from the 2027 season.

The five-year agreement covers both the men’s and women’s senior teams and is one of the biggest commercial partnerships in the history of the Tallaght-based club.

The partnership goes well beyond the standard shirt sponsorship model, with the two organisations committing to a range of fan engagement initiatives, community activities and exclusive supporter experiences.

There will also be a significant retail element to the relationship with the new Shamrock Rovers kit going on sale via nine Sports Direct stores across Dublin and Kildare, giving the club a much broader high street presence.

The financial terms of the agreement have not been disclosed.

“We’re absolutely delighted to be welcoming Sports Direct as our new Front of Shirt partner’ said CEO Robbie Hedderman.

“This is one of the most significant commercial deals in the history of the club, and it reflects the ambition we have for Shamrock Rovers both on and off the pitch.”

“Sports Direct is a brand that shares our belief in the power of sport to bring people together, and it is very important to us that their name will be on the front of the shirt worn by both our Men’s and Women’s senior teams.”

“Beyond the shirt, we’re very excited to be working with Sports Direct on a number of new initiatives to support our fans and to extend the reach of our Community Foundation from Tallaght and beyond.”

The deal sees another property added to Sports Direct’s significant investment in Irish sport, as part of its wider programme of sponsorship across Gaelic games and football.

“As one of the most iconic and successful clubs in Irish football, we’re very excited to be embarking on this new chapter with Shamrock Rovers,” said Leonard Brassel, Managing Director at Sports Direct Ireland.

“Together we want to create opportunities for the fans, support the wider community and help inspire more people to get involved in sport.”

The new 2027 kit will be available in Sports Direct stores at The Square Tallaght, Henry Street, Liffey Valley, Blanchardstown, Carrickmines, Finglas, Maynooth, Naas and Newbridge.

It’ll also be available from the club store at Tallaght Stadium in December, of course, capitalising on the key Christmas retail period.

A five-year commitment from a major international retailer is another clear vote of confidence in the League of Ireland’s commercial direction and gives Shamrock Rovers a degree of financial certainty to build on.

The fact that both senior teams are in is a good thing, and the commitment to the Shamrock Rovers Community Foundation’s work is obviously a positive.

The retail side is the most interesting. Getting League of Ireland merchandise into mainstream sports goods stores alongside the merchandise of big international clubs would be a massive boost to the game’s profile and would expose the club to a whole new audience.

Competition between brands for a foothold in Irish football is obviously increasing, and this deal is another clear sign of the commercialisation of the domestic game.

title: Ajax reunite with ABN AMRO in five-year sponsorship agreement
article_text:
AFC Ajax have announced a five-year partnership with Dutch banking group ABN AMRO, which will become the club’s new main sponsor from the 2027-28 season.

The agreement marks the return of a long-standing commercial partner to the front of Ajax’s shirts, nearly two decades after the bank ended its previous stint as the club’s principal sponsor.

Set to commence on July 1, 2027, the agreement will run until the end of the 2031-32 season and cover Ajax’s men’s first team, Women’s first team and Jong Ajax. The banking group will replace telecommunications company Ziggo, whose sponsorship arrangement concludes after the 2026-27 season.

The partnership reunites two organisations with a shared history spanning 35 years. ABN AMRO previously served as Ajax’s main shirt sponsor between 1991 and 2008, a period that included the club’s 1995 UEFA Champions League triumph. The bank has since maintained its association through its involvement with Ajax Women, the youth academy and community initiatives.

Menno Geelen, CEO of Ajax, said, “This is very good news for the club. We are delighted to have found a new main sponsor in ABN AMRO following an intensive and carefully considered process. We have been connected for decades, and this main sponsorship will feel familiar to everyone within the club and to our supporters. We are grateful to ABN AMRO for their confidence in our future.”

Marguerite Bérard, CEO of ABN AMRO, added, “We are proud that ABN AMRO will soon feature on the Ajax shirt again as main sponsor, for both the men’s and women’s teams. We have celebrated great successes together, and we have been committed to this partnership for thirty-five years. That rich history is the foundation for a new beginning.”

Cas Biesta, CCO of Ajax, continued, “We are very pleased that ABN AMRO will become our new main sponsor. When looking for a main sponsor, you want to strike a balance between what is a good fit for the club and what makes sense commercially. It is therefore wonderful to have found a main sponsor that delivers on both fronts. Building on our rich shared history, we want to write a successful future together. We will develop an impactful partnership that creates value for the club and its supporters, as well as for ABN AMRO and its clients and business partners.”

Geert Pielage, Head of Brand and Corporate Communications at ABN AMRO, shared, “The Ajax shirt bearing ABN AMRO brings back special memories for many people. We are proud of that. But we do not just want to recall who we were together; we want to show what we stand for today: helping people and businesses move forward. Our longstanding involvement with Ajax’s women’s team and youth academy, along with our community partnership, already puts this into practice. With this main sponsorship, we want to strengthen that connection. Not just recognisable on the shirt, but meaningful on and off the pitch.”

The agreement strengthens Ajax’s commercial relationship with an established domestic brand while giving ABN AMRO an expanded presence across the club’s footballing and community structures.

title: Shorts: Sky, Newcastle Red Bulls, PWR
article_text:
Sky has brought together leaders from sport, broadcasting, business and politics to launch the Game Changing Coalition. Its aim is to close the gap between girls’ and boys’ participation in sport.

Chaired by former Sports Minister Dame Tracey Crouch, the coalition held its first meeting this week. Founding members include Sky Sports CEO Jonathan Licht, WSL Football CEO Nikki Doucet, the Premier League’s Chief Football Officer Rebecca Caplehorn, the ECB’s Chief Revenue Officer Aarti Dabas and Judy Murray. They are joined by Baroness Sue Campbell, Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson, Anita Asante and Ebony-Jewel Rainford-Brent, alongside senior figures from The FA, World Rugby, UEFA, Nike, YouTube, Deloitte, Barclays, Howden Group and Mumsnet.

According to Sky’s Game Changing report, girls spend 1.4 fewer hours a week playing sport than boys, the equivalent of missing 52 football matches a year. Coalition members reach more than 750 million people through their platforms and together invest millions each year in sport, physical activity and grassroots programmes.

The coalition will work across three pillars, Play, Watch and Attend, and will set clear, accountable goals. Constituency-level research will help it target the communities with the lowest participation. With the UK set to host the 2031 Netball World Cup and the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup, the group also aims to help build a lasting legacy from both tournaments. Sky will revisit its research at the end of 2028 to measure progress.

Dame Tracey Crouch, Chair of the Game Changing Coalition, said, “Despite many excellent initiatives, progress in women’s sport remains stubbornly static. What makes this coalition different is the unique mix of voices lending their influence, expertise and resources to the cause that can help drive meaningful change. By harnessing that collective power with commercial backing, we can break down barriers at scale and ensure every girl, regardless of her background or where she lives, has the opportunity to get active and stay active.”

Jonathan Licht, CEO of Sky Sports, said, “Too many girls are experiencing barriers to playing sport, and the result is 280 million missing hours of sport a year compared to boys. Closing that gap isn’t just about getting more girls active, it’s about giving them the opportunity to build confidence, make connections and develop skills that will benefit them throughout their lives. That is why we are using Sky’s unique position in the UK to bring together sporting and commercial organisations with the influence to drive lasting change.”

Sky is also supporting The Equal Sport Project, which launched on 10th November with the ambition of making the UK the world’s leading nation for women and girls’ sport.

Newcastle Red Bulls have signed Destination Sport as their travel supplier in a multi-year deal, starting with a chance for supporters to fly with the team to Lyon in the EPCR Challenge Cup.

Destination Sport is a global travel business built for sport, with a portfolio of specialist brands connecting teams, rights holders, events, fans and participants. The partnership brings together its elite team travel and fan experience expertise, with plans to expand into youth development tours.

The first trip, organised through Destination Sport’s fan travel brand SportsBreaks, takes supporters to Newcastle’s Challenge Cup match against LOU Rugby at Matmut Stadium on Sunday 17th January 2027. Packages include return flights on the team charter from Newcastle, one night’s accommodation, airport and stadium transfers and staff support. Bookings close on Thursday 3rd December.

The deal adds to a run of partnerships at Kingston Park, following the recent arrival of Thatchers as cider partner and Ad Gefrin as whisky supplier.

Jonny Petrie, Managing Director of Newcastle Red Bulls, said, “We’re delighted to welcome Destination Sport as our Official Travel Supplier. They have a wealth of experience in professional team travel and fan experiences, and we look forward to working with them to build on this expertise to develop our supporter travel offering.“

“Our trip to Lyon in January is a great way to get things started, giving our supporters the opportunity to travel with the team, get behind the lads in Europe and make their presence felt away from home.”

Steve Butchart, Managing Director of Elite & Youth at Destination Sport, said, “We are delighted to announce this new multi-year agreement with Newcastle Red Bulls. This is a partnership that really demonstrates the breadth of Destination Sport’s offering, bringing together specialist expertise in elite team travel and fan experiences, with a view to expanding into youth development tours under one joined-up solution.

“Newcastle Red Bulls is a club with a proud heritage and exciting ambition for the future, and we’re excited to bring our specialist travel services to the club to help support that ambition over the coming years.”

English sparkling wine producer Nyetimber has become sponsor of the Player of the Match award in Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR), extending its partnership portfolio in English rugby.

Across all 21 rounds of the 2026/27 JAECOO PWR season, each Player of the Match will receive a magnum of Nyetimber Classic Cuvee Multi-Vintage.

Nyetimber was the first to plant the classic sparkling wine grape varieties in the UK, in 1988. Its Head Winemaker, Cherie Spriggs, became the first woman and the first person from outside Champagne to be named Sparkling Winemaker of the Year at the International Wine Challenge in 2018. She won the award again in 2025 and remains the only woman to have done so.

The PWR deal builds on Nyetimber’s wider support for the sport. The brand became England Rugby’s sparkling wine partner in 2025 and is served at all England home matches at Allianz Stadium. It also sponsors Richmond Rugby and has signed England captain Jamie George as a brand ambassador.

title: Rivers United sign three-year N490m shirt sponsorship deal
article_text:
Rivers United have signed a three-year front-of-shirt sponsorship deal worth $350,000 (about N490 million) with Goka Sports and Casino, as the club seeks to strengthen its commercial base amid its push for the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) title.

The agreement was unveiled on Tuesday at Platinum Hall, Hotel Presidential, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

The club’s sole administrator, Christopher Green, said Rivers United rejected Goka’s initial proposal for a one-year agreement, opting instead for a three-year commitment with an upward renewal option.

“Goka wanted a one-year contract with an extension, but we said no. We’ll go for three years first, with an upward renewal.

“So the deal is worth three hundred and fifty thousand US dollars, which is four hundred and ninety million naira in Nigerian currency,” Mr Green said.

The deal comes as Rivers United continue to establish themselves among the leading sides in Nigerian football. The club finished second in last season’s NPFL, narrowly missing out on the title by one point after accumulating 67 points from 38 matches, compared with champions Rangers International’s 68.

The Port Harcourt club have maintained their competitive form this season, remaining in the title race and keeping pressure on the teams above them. Their performances have reinforced their ambition to challenge for the league crown again.

Mr Green said the sponsorship could pave the way for additional commercial agreements covering other parts of the team’s kit, including the back of the shirt and sleeves.

“With this, we’ve opened the door for more sponsorship deals. In no time, we will get the one for the back shirt, one for the sleeve and the others,” he said.

He also disclosed that discussions were ongoing to extend Goka’s involvement to Rivers Hoopers, the state’s basketball team.

“We have been talking to Goka and we have also sold Rivers Hoopers to them. Soon they will come for the same front-shirt sponsorship,” he said.

Speaking on behalf of Goka Sports and Casino, Jide Odi described the agreement as a significant commitment to Nigerian sports, saying the company assessed several clubs before settling on Rivers United.

He said the assessment considered the clubs’ history, coefficients and standing in domestic football.

“We’re here to stay, we’re not going anywhere.

“Goka is here to expand the frontiers of private partnership with sports in Nigeria, and we’re starting with Rivers United,” Mr Odi said.

He said the club’s ambitions aligned with the company’s plan to expand private-sector involvement in Nigerian sports, adding that the partnership was expected to create opportunities for both sides.

Mr Odi expressed regret that the unveiling did not take place before Rivers United’s 6-0 victory over Niger Tornadoes, saying he would have liked to see the new branding on the club’s shirts during the match.

He, however, said the agreement was intended to be a long-term relationship.

“This is just the first step in the long-term relationship. We’re looking to expand the conversation in partnerships and to see how we can take Nigerian football forward,” he said.

Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara, represented at the event by former Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Communications, Mike Elechi, commended the club’s management for securing the agreement.

Mr Elechi said the partnership represented an investment in the club, noting that the sponsors would also need to recoup their investment through commercial activities, including jersey sales.

He also thanked Goka for choosing Rivers United, describing the partnership as an opportunity to support the club’s development.

title: Qualcomm links F1 sponsorship to measurable ROI
article_text:
Qualcomm is presenting its Formula 1 marketing as more than a prestige exercise. Through its Snapdragon consumer brand, the company says its partnership with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS Formula 1 team is producing measurable brand impact and, in the short term, higher return on investment (ROI) from selected activations. The approach marks a deliberate shift from Qualcomm’s earlier F1 involvement, which its chief marketing officer says was not designed around marketing ROI.

The latest evidence of that strategy is Snapdragon’s campaign with Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, launched ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. It combines a driver-led creative platform with broadcast, digital and social distribution, while Qualcomm continues to measure the partnership against awareness, engagement and brand-lift metrics rather than relying solely on logo exposure.

Qualcomm’s current F1 strategy is built around Snapdragon, the company’s consumer-facing brand for mobile, computing and connected-device technologies. The company’s broader challenge has been familiar to many business-to-business technology firms: its chips may be embedded in millions of devices, but the brand itself has historically had limited direct recognition among consumers.

Snapdragon’s partnership with Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS began in 2023 as a multi-year collaboration. Qualcomm had previously worked with Mercedes in the 2010s, but Don McGuire, Qualcomm’s chief marketing officer since 2021, has described that earlier arrangement as not being “ROI-driven” or “marketing-driven.” The renewed relationship was therefore designed to connect sponsorship activity more directly to commercial and brand objectives.

That distinction matters because F1 sponsorship can deliver highly visible placements on cars, driver suits, garage branding and onboard camera assets but those impressions are often brief. McGuire has said that placements such as cockpit cameras are “fleeting” from a visibility standpoint, making advertising-value-equivalency alone an inadequate way to judge the value of the investment.

Instead, Qualcomm frames F1 as a platform for a longer brand-building journey. Its stated objective is to move consumers from awareness of Snapdragon, through consideration, toward purchase intent for Snapdragon-powered products such as smartphones, PCs and connected cars.

Qualcomm has not publicly disclosed a precise financial ROI figure, revenue uplift, sales conversion rate or sponsorship cost for its Mercedes partnership. Its claims should therefore be understood as management statements about marketing performance rather than independently audited financial results.

Still, the company has identified the indicators it uses. Garrett Ponder, Qualcomm’s director of marketing, has said the company sets and benchmarks key performance indicators including awareness, engagement and brand lift against its wider marketing activity. It works with CAA Brand Consulting to establish those benchmarks and assess performance.

Qualcomm says it has already observed a “meaningful, statistically significant lift in brand metrics” from the Mercedes partnership. In a 2024 blog post, McGuire also said that investments including sponsorship had helped drive awareness at twice the competitive average and contributed to demand for Snapdragon devices. Those statements describe broad sponsorship-related marketing effects, not a clean attribution of every result to F1 alone.

The company’s approach is therefore less about claiming that a logo on a race car directly produced a measurable sales number, and more about using F1 as a high-reach environment in which to build recognition and emotional association for Snapdragon. That is consistent with Qualcomm’s broader effort to make its technology “visible and emotionally resonant” to consumers.

Formula 1 offers Qualcomm a global audience that the company sees as aligned with its target markets. Ponder has said the sport’s fanbase skews younger and is more tech-savvy than many other major sports properties. Qualcomm has also identified China and India as key mobile markets, while the United States, United Kingdom and Germany are important markets for its computing business.

The Mercedes partnership gives Snapdragon visibility in those markets, but Qualcomm has emphasized that it does not treat the deal as a simple branding exercise. The company uses driver access, fan-facing storytelling, hospitality and race-weekend activations to create more durable engagement.

Hospitality remains a significant part of the Mercedes relationship. Qualcomm runs programmes for clients and special guests at several races during the season, which Ponder has described as impactful for the business. These activations can support commercial relationships and give Qualcomm a more direct setting in which to discuss its technology with customers and partners.

At the same time, the company has tried to avoid content that feels imposed on the sport. One example cited by BlackBook Motorsport was Snapdragon’s 2025 response to FIA guidance on driver swearing: the brand created a piece featuring George Russell using a stand-in swearing double while discussing Snapdragon technology. Qualcomm positioned such work as fan-led and tied to conversations already happening within the sport.

The most recent campaign centers on Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS driver whom Snapdragon signed as a brand ambassador. Marketing Dive reported that Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 World Champion earlier in November 2026, shortly before Snapdragon launched an anthem film around him.

The campaign was timed to the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 21. Its 60-second hero video follows Antonelli through a day at a hotel, showing him wearing Snapdragon-powered smart glasses and using a Snapdragon-powered tablet. He listens to a version of the traditional Neapolitan song “Funiculì, Funiculà,” trains in a gym and helps start a social-media trend. The campaign closes with the tagline, “Jamme, Jamme. To the top!”

The distribution strategy is notable because it reflects the constraints of F1’s U.S. broadcast arrangements. Apple TV is the exclusive U.S. broadcast partner for Formula 1, which prevents Snapdragon from running traditional broadcast advertisements around races in that market. Qualcomm has therefore used F1 broadcasts outside the United States through Sky, along with digital channels, YouTube and a partnership with Sports Illustrated.
